title: Tranylcypromine shows in-vitro activity against Leishmania major
summary: The study experimentally tested the previously model-predicted drug tranylcypromine against L. major promastigotes and intracellular amastigotes. It reports IC50 values of 83.6 and 31.6 µg/mL, respectively, and macrophage CC50 of 282.3 µg/mL. These relatively high in-vitro concentrations do not establish achievable exposure, patient safety or clinical efficacy; human monoamine oxidase mechanism is not shown as the parasite target.
ai_technology: Prior machine-learning drug-repurposing pipeline (the present study is experimental validation)
organization: Institut Pasteur de Tunis; Université de Tunis El Manar

evidence.tested: Primary full text reports promastigote and intracellular amastigote assays with dose responses and host-cell cytotoxicity.
evidence.unknown: Prior drug/species work, tolerability and mechanism remain unresolved; no clinical inference.
evidence.ai_role: Study experimentally validates a model-prioritized repurposing candidate from earlier research.
